questions.q: A particle accelerates uniformly from \(u=2\) m/s to \(v=14\) m/s over \(6\) seconds, then travels at constant velocity for a further \(4\) seconds. The velocity-time graph is shown. Find the total distance traveled, using the area under the graph.
questions.answer: Distance in first phase (trapezoid): \(\frac{1}{2}(2+14)(6)=48\) m. Distance in second phase (rectangle): \(14\times4=56\) m. Total: \(48+56=104\) m.

questions.answer: The graph forms a right triangle with base \(5\) and height \(20\). Distance \(=\frac{1}{2}(5)(20)=50\) m.

questions.q: Two cars start 300 meters apart on a straight road and travel toward each other, one at \(18\) m/s and the other at \(12\) m/s, both at constant speed. Find the time until they meet.
questions.answer: Combined closing speed: \(18+12=30\) m/s. Time \(=\frac{300}{30}=10\) seconds.
questions.explanation: Combined closing speed: \(18+12=30\) m/s. Time \(=\frac{300}{30}=10\) seconds.

questions.q: Two cars start at the same point on a straight road, one traveling at \(25\) m/s. The second car starts 4 seconds later, traveling at \(30\) m/s. Find how long after the first car starts the second car catches up.
questions.answer: Let \(t\) be the time (seconds) after the first car starts. First car's position: \(25t\). Second car's position (starting 4 s later): \(30(t-4)\). Setting equal: \(25t=30(t-4)=30t-120\), so \(5t=120\), giving \(t=24\) seconds.

Two particles \(P\) of mass \(3\mathrm{\ kg}\) and \(Q\) of mass \(5\mathrm{\ kg}\) are connected by a light inextensible string passing over a smooth fixed pulley. The system is held at rest and released. Taking \(g = 9.8\mathrm{\ m/s}^2\): (a) find the acceleration \(a\) of the system, (b) calculate the tension \(T\) in the string, (c) find the force exerted by the string on the pulley.
questions.target: A well-designed word problem: a train between two stations
questions.answer: (a) Write \(F = ma\) for each particle in its direction of motion: For \(Q\) (moving downwards): \(5g - T = 5a\) For \(P\) (moving upwards): \(T - 3g = 3a\) Add the equations: \(2g = 8a \Rightarrow a = \frac{2(9.8)}{8} = 2.45\mathrm{\ m/s}^2\) (b) Substitute \(a\) into the equation for \(P\): \(T = 3g + 3a = 3(9.8 + 2.45) = 3(12.25) = 36.75\mathrm{\ N} \approx 36.8\mathrm{\ N}\) (c) The pulley supports two vertical segments of string with tension \(T\), so the total downward force on the pulley is: \(F_{\mathrm{pulley}} = 2T = 2(36.75) = 73.5\mathrm{\ N}\)

questions.q: A particle moves so that its velocity at time \( t \) s (\( t\geq0 \)) is \( v=2t^{2}-2t \) m/s. Find when the particle is momentarily at rest.

A stone is thrown vertically upwards with speed \(15\mathrm{\ m/s}\) from the top of a cliff \(40\mathrm{\ m}\) above sea level. Taking \(g = 9.8\mathrm{\ m/s}^2\) and upwards as positive: (a) find the maximum height reached above the cliff, (b) calculate the time taken for the stone to reach the sea.
questions.answer: (a) At maximum height, \(v = 0\). \(u = +15\mathrm{\ m/s}\), \(a = -9.8\mathrm{\ m/s}^2\): \(v^2 = u^2 + 2as \Rightarrow 0 = 15^2 + 2(-9.8)s \Rightarrow 19.6s = 225 \Rightarrow s = \frac{225}{19.6} \approx 11.48\mathrm{\ m} \approx 11.5\mathrm{\ m}\) (b) At the sea, the displacement relative to the launch point is \(s = -40\mathrm{\ m}\). Use \(s = ut + \frac{1}{2}at^2\): \(-40 = 15t + \frac{1}{2}(-9.8)t^2 \Rightarrow -40 = 15t - 4.9t^2 \Rightarrow 4.9t^2 - 15t - 40 = 0\) Solve via quadratic formula: \(t = \frac{15 \pm \sqrt{(-15)^2 - 4(4.9)(-40)}}{2(4.9)} = \frac{15 \pm \sqrt{225 + 784}}{9.8} = \frac{15 \pm \sqrt{1009}}{9.8}\) Since \(\sqrt{1009} \approx 31.765\), and \(t > 0\): \(t = \frac{15 + 31.765}{9.8} = \frac{46.765}{9.8} \approx 4.77\mathrm{\ s\ (3\ s.f.)}\)
questions.explanation: (a) At maximum height, \(v = 0\). \(u = +15\mathrm{\ m/s}\), \(a = -9.8\mathrm{\ m/s}^2\): \(v^2 = u^2 + 2as \Rightarrow 0 = 15^2 + 2(-9.8)s \Rightarrow 19.6s = 225 \Rightarrow s = \frac{225}{19.6} \approx 11.48\mathrm{\ m} \approx 11.5\mathrm{\ m}\) (b) At the sea, the displacement relative to the launch point is \(s = -40\mathrm{\ m}\). Use \(s = ut + \frac{1}{2}at^2\): \(-40 = 15t + \frac{1}{2}(-9.8)t^2 \Rightarrow -40 = 15t - 4.9t^2 \Rightarrow 4.9t^2 - 15t - 40 = 0\) Solve via quadratic formula: \(t = \frac{15 \pm \sqrt{(-15)^2 - 4(4.9)(-40)}}{2(4.9)} = \frac{15 \pm \sqrt{225 + 784}}{9.8} = \frac{15 \pm \sqrt{1009}}{9.8}\) Since \(\sqrt{1009} \approx 31.765\), and \(t > 0\): \(t = \frac{15 + 31.765}{9.8} = \frac{46.765}{9.8} \approx 4.77\mathrm{\ s\ (3\ s.f.)}\)

questions.q: A particle has initial velocity \(u=4\) m/s and constant acceleration \(a=4\) m/s\(^2\). Find its displacement after \(t=6\) s.

A particle moves in a straight line such that its displacement \(s\) metres from a fixed origin after \(t\) seconds is given by the equation \(s = t^3 - 6t^2 + 9t + 2\). The velocity of the particle is given by \(v = \frac{ds}{dt}\). Find the value of \(t\) for which the particle is instantaneously at rest and then determine the displacement of the particle at that instant.
questions.answer: The displacement is given by \(s = t^3 - 6t^2 + 9t + 2\). To find the velocity, we differentiate the displacement with respect to time: \(v = \frac{ds}{dt} = \frac{d}{dt}(t^3 - 6t^2 + 9t + 2) = 3t^2 - 12t + 9\). The particle is instantaneously at rest when its velocity is zero, i.e., \(v=0\). So, we set the velocity equation to zero: \(3t^2 - 12t + 9 = 0\). Divide by 3: \(t^2 - 4t + 3 = 0\). Factorize the quadratic equation: \((t-1)(t-3) = 0\). This gives two possible values for \(t\): \(t=1\) or \(t=3\). The question asks for 'the value of \(t\) for which the particle is instantaneously at rest', implying a single specific instant or asking to consider all such instants. In the context of exam questions, when a specific value is sought after and multiple arise, the problem usually intends for the student to analyze further or there's a subtle implication. However, given the structure of finding displacement *at that instant*, it is likely asking for one of these specific times. Let's evaluate the displacement for both. If \(t=1\) second: \(s = (1)^3 - 6(1)^2 + 9(1) + 2 = 1 - 6 + 9 + 2 = 6\) metres. If \(t=3\) seconds: \(s = (3)^3 - 6(3)^2 + 9(3) + 2 = 27 - 6(9) + 27 + 2 = 27 - 54 + 27 + 2 = 2\) metres. The question implies finding *a* value of t and the corresponding displacement. Common algebraic traps might involve selecting only one of the roots or miscalculating the displacement. Both \(t=1\) and \(t=3\) represent instants when the particle is at rest. The question then asks for 'the displacement of the particle at that instant'. This can be interpreted as finding the displacement for one of the times the particle is at rest. Since both are valid, we check the options. Option C provides \(t=3\) s, \(s=2\) m, which is one of the valid pairs. Common Misconceptions: 1. Forgetting to differentiate correctly: Leads to incorrect velocity equation. 2. Errors in solving the quadratic equation: Missing roots or solving incorrectly. 3. Selecting the wrong time value if not considering all possibilities or misinterpreting the question. 4. Calculation errors when substituting \(t\) back into the displacement equation.

questions.q: A particle moves so that its velocity at time \( t \) s (\( t\geq0 \)) is \( v=2t^{2}-10t \) m/s. Find when the particle is momentarily at rest.

A particle of mass 5 kg is at rest on a smooth horizontal surface. A constant horizontal force of magnitude 20 N is applied to the particle. What is the magnitude of the acceleration of the particle in m/s\(^2\)?
questions.target: Finding when a particle is at rest or changes direction
questions.answer: According to Newton's Second Law of Motion, the net force acting on an object is equal to the product of its mass and acceleration, i.e., \(F = ma\). Given: Mass \(m = 5\) kg, Force \(F = 20\) N. We need to find the acceleration \(a\). Rearranging the formula, \(a = \frac{F}{m}\). Substituting the given values: \(a = \frac{20 \mathrm{\ N}}{5 \mathrm{\ kg}} = 4 \mathrm{\ m/s}^2\). Therefore, the magnitude of the acceleration of the particle is 4 m/s\(^2\).

Substituting the given values: \(a = \frac{20 \mathrm{\ N}}{5 \mathrm{\ kg}} = 4 \mathrm{\ m/s}^2\). Therefore, the magnitude of the acceleration of the particle is 4 m/s\(^2\).

questions.q: In an applied problem, a particle moves so that its velocity at time \( t \) s (\( t\geq0 \)) is \( v=3t^{2}-15t \) m/s. Find when the particle is momentarily at rest.

Two particles, A and B, move in the xy-plane. Their position vectors at time \(t\) seconds, for \(t \geq 0\), are given by \(\mathbf{r}_A(t) = \left(2t ; 4t - 1\right)\) and \(\mathbf{r}_B(t) = \left(3 + 5t ; 1 - 2t\right)\) respectively. The particles start their motion at \(t=0\). Find the minimum distance between particle A and particle B.
questions.answer: The position vectors of particle A and particle B at time \(t\) are given by \(\mathbf{r}_A(t) = \left(2t ; 4t - 1\right)\) and \(\mathbf{r}_B(t) = \left(3 + 5t ; 1 - 2t\right)\). The vector representing the displacement from particle B to particle A at time \(t\) is \(\mathbf{d}(t) = \mathbf{r}_A(t) - \mathbf{r}_B(t) = \left(2t - (3 + 5t) ; (4t - 1) - (1 - 2t)\right) = \left(-3t - 3 ; 6t - 2\right)\). The distance between the particles at time \(t\) is the magnitude of this displacement vector, \(D(t) = ||\mathbf{d}(t)|| = \sqrt{(-3t - 3)^2 + (6t - 2)^2}\). To minimize the distance, we can minimize the square of the distance, \(D(t)^2 = (-3t - 3)^2 + (6t - 2)^2\). Let \(f(t) = D(t)^2 = (9t^2 + 18t + 9) + (36t^2 - 24t + 4) = 45t^2 - 6t + 13\). This is a quadratic function of \(t\), representing a parabola opening upwards. The minimum value occurs at the vertex. The t-coordinate of the vertex is given by \(t = -\frac{b}{2a}\), where \(a=45\) and \(b=-6\). So, \(t = -\frac{-6}{2 \times 45} = \frac{6}{90} = \frac{1}{15}\). Now, substitute this value of \(t\) back into the expression for \(D(t)^2\) to find the minimum squared distance: \(f(\frac{1}{15}) = 45(\frac{1}{15})^2 - 6(\frac{1}{15}) + 13 = 45(\frac{1}{225}) - \frac{6}{15} + 13 = \frac{1}{5} - \frac{2}{5} + 13 = -\frac{1}{5} + 13 = \frac{-1 + 65}{5} = \frac{64}{5}\). The minimum distance is the square root of the minimum squared distance: \(D_{min} = \sqrt{\frac{64}{5}} = \frac{8}{\sqrt{5}} = \frac{8\sqrt{5}}{5}\).
questions.explanation: The position vectors of particle A and particle B at time \(t\) are given by \(\mathbf{r}_A(t) = \left(2t ; 4t - 1\right)\) and \(\mathbf{r}_B(t) = \left(3 + 5t ; 1 - 2t\right)\). The vector representing the displacement from particle B to particle A at time \(t\) is \(\mathbf{d}(t) = \mathbf{r}_A(t) - \mathbf{r}_B(t) = \left(2t - (3 + 5t) ; (4t - 1) - (1 - 2t)\right) = \left(-3t - 3 ; 6t - 2\right)\). The distance between the particles at time \(t\) is the magnitude of this displacement vector, \(D(t) = ||\mathbf{d}(t)|| = \sqrt{(-3t - 3)^2 + (6t - 2)^2}\). To minimize the distance, we can minimize the square of the distance, \(D(t)^2 = (-3t - 3)^2 + (6t - 2)^2\). Let \(f(t) = D(t)^2 = (9t^2 + 18t + 9) + (36t^2 - 24t + 4) = 45t^2 - 6t + 13\). This is a quadratic function of \(t\), representing a parabola opening upwards. The minimum value occurs at the vertex. The t-coordinate of the vertex is given by \(t = -\frac{b}{2a}\), where \(a=45\) and \(b=-6\). So, \(t = -\frac{-6}{2 \times 45} = \frac{6}{90} = \frac{1}{15}\). Now, substitute this value of \(t\) back into the expression for \(D(t)^2\) to find the minimum squared distance: \(f(\frac{1}{15}) = 45(\frac{1}{15})^2 - 6(\frac{1}{15}) + 13 = 45(\frac{1}{225}) - \frac{6}{15} + 13 = \frac{1}{5} - \frac{2}{5} + 13 = -\frac{1}{5} + 13 = \frac{-1 + 65}{5} = \frac{64}{5}\). The minimum distance is the square root of the minimum squared distance: \(D_{min} = \sqrt{\frac{64}{5}} = \frac{8}{\sqrt{5}} = \frac{8\sqrt{5}}{5}\).

A particle in equilibrium is acted on by three concurrent forces. Two of the forces have equal magnitude \(20\) N and act symmetrically either side of the third force's line of action. If the angle between each of the two equal forces and the third force is \(120^\circ\), find the magnitude of the third force.
questions.answer: By symmetry (each pair at \(120^\circ\)), the third force balances the resultant of the two equal forces: \(F_3=F_1=20\) N (standard \(120^\circ\)-\(120^\circ\)-\(120^\circ\) symmetric equilibrium).
questions.explanation: By symmetry (each pair at \(120^\circ\)), the third force balances the resultant of the two equal forces: \(F_3=F_1=20\) N (standard \(120^\circ\)-\(120^\circ\)-\(120^\circ\) symmetric equilibrium).

questions.q: Particles of mass \(2\) kg and \(5\) kg are connected by a light inextensible string over a smooth pulley, and released from rest. Taking \(g=9.8\) m/s\(^2\), find the acceleration of the system.
A particle accelerates uniformly from \(u=2\) m/s to \(v=14\) m/s in \(t=6\) s. Find its acceleration.
A particle has initial velocity \( u=2 \) m/s and constant acceleration \( a=2 \) m/s\(^2\). Find its displacement after \( t=5 \) s.
A particle moves so that its velocity at time \( t \) s is \( v=2t \) m/s. Find the acceleration at \( t=2 \) s.

A particle moves in a straight line with acceleration \(a(t) = 6t - 8 \mathrm{\ m/s}^2\). If it starts from rest at the origin (at \(t = 0\)), at what time \(t > 0\) does the particle momentarily come to rest again?
questions.answer: Velocity \(v(t) = \int (6t - 8)\,dt = 3t^2 - 8t + C\). Since \(v(0) = 0 \Rightarrow C = 0\). Momentarily at rest when \(v(t) = 0 \Rightarrow t(3t - 8) = 0 \Rightarrow t = \frac{8}{3} \mathrm{\ s}\).
questions.explanation: Velocity \(v(t) = \int (6t - 8)\,dt = 3t^2 - 8t + C\). Since \(v(0) = 0 \Rightarrow C = 0\). Momentarily at rest when \(v(t) = 0 \Rightarrow t(3t - 8) = 0 \Rightarrow t = \frac{8}{3} \mathrm{\ s}\).

questions.q: A constant force of 15 N is applied to an object, causing it to move a distance of 4 m in the direction of the force. Calculate the work done by the force.
questions.target: A well-designed word problem: a train between two stations
questions.answer: The work done by a constant force is given by the formula: Work Done = Force × Distance × cos(θ) where θ is the angle between the force and the direction of motion. In this case, the force and the distance are in the same direction, so θ = 0°. Therefore, cos(0°) = 1. Work Done = 15 N × 4 m × 1 Work Done = 60 J

questions.q: Three concurrent forces keep a particle in equilibrium, each pair separated by \(120^\circ\), and two of the forces have magnitude \(28\) N. Find the magnitude of the third force.
questions.answer: With all three angles equal to \(120^\circ\), Lami's theorem gives \(\frac{F_1}{\sin120^\circ}=\frac{F_2}{\sin120^\circ}=\frac{F_3}{\sin120^\circ} \Rightarrow F_3=F_1=28\) N.
